label: copy-phase input k, late in the copy (sparse subset)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input token is k (100% of activations have in_tok == k). It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token. Activations are concentrated late in long sequences: recall_idx >= 4 covers 94% of activations and 96% of mass, and L == 9 holds 74% of mass. The largest activations come when k is the second-to-last or last copied input of a length-9 sequence. Magnitude is also higher when the token being output next is f or r (and to a lesser degree k, p, z). Still, even with these conditions the feature is very sparse: only about 4% of late copy-phase k inputs activate it (dev precision 0.04). Adding out_tok in {f, r} raises precision only to about 0.2 and drops recall to 0.32. The rule that decides WHICH late k inputs fire was not found; prev_tok and other history variables give only weak lift.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=k (+5.38), in_tok=k (+3.51), phase=2 & out_tok=r (+3.15), recall_idx=8 & in_tok=k (+2.82), next_out=f (+2.67), phase=2 & out_tok=k (+2.26). Lower it: out_tok=0 (-2.81), prev2_tok=<DEL> (-2.52), recall_idx=2 (-2.52), recall_idx=1 (-2.18).
